description: The plot illustrates how the maximum activation value varies across model layers for four series labeled “attn_output,” “attn_residual,” “ffn_output,” and “ffn_residual.” The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0 to 23 with major ticks shown at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Max Activation Value,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to about 1600 with regularly spaced tick labels every 200 units. The “attn_output” line is blue with a dashed style and no markers; it stays near 0 for most layers and then rises late, reaching roughly ~250 by the final layer. The “attn_residual” line is orange with a dotted style and no markers; it is near 0 through about layer 4, jumps to around ~1400 at about layer 6, increases to around ~1500–1600 by roughly layers 14–16, stays near ~1600 through about layer 21–22, and then drops sharply near the end to roughly ~250 at the final layer. The “ffn_output” line is green with a dash-dot style and no markers; it is near 0 early, spikes to about ~1400 around layer 5, falls back near 0 by around layers 7–11, spikes again around layer 13 to roughly ~800, returns to low values (tens) through the mid-to-late layers, and then spikes again near layer 22 to roughly ~1200 before ending around ~600 at the final layer. The “ffn_residual” line is red with a solid style and no markers; it is near 0 through about layer 4, jumps to about ~1400 at layer ~5, rises to around ~1500 by about layer 7, remains near ~1500 through roughly layer 12, increases to about ~1600 by around layers 14–16, stays near ~1600 through about layer 21, then drops sharply near layer 22 to roughly ~400 and ends around ~600 at the final layer.
